newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 8.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Labour leader Helen Clark was judged a two-time winner by undecided voters operating an electronic "worm" in the final TVNZ leaders' debate with Alliance leader Jim Anderton a close second. The debate, controversial because of the use of the worm and the inclusion of three minor party leaders, did little to salvage National's flailing election campaign. Prime Minister Jim Bolger registered less than half Clark's score. Political strategists agreed the debate would be highly influential in shaping the climate of the closing days of the election campaign. Page 1.
A woman with an air pistol has been arrested after seeking a meeting with former prime minister David Lange. Page 1.

New Zealand First's Wellington Central candidate, Sarah Porter, has conceded an early defeat and urged supporters to switch their electorate votes to the Labour or National candidates to stop ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble being elected. Recent polls show Prebble is closing in on the frontrunning National candidate in the Wellington Central electorate. Page 2.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger softened his tone but continued to predict gloom if National did not retain the Treasury benches on October 12. Page 2.

Concern among church leaders is growing about the effect of some of the Christian Coalition's moral right-leaning policies. And they are concerned about the use of the word "Christian" because of its association with churches. Page 2.

The share market continued to ignore political polls and baffle brokers yesterday as it strode ahead to close on a two and a half year high of 2,274.76, up 30.48 points. Telcom led the way, gaining another 15 cents on Friday's record to finish the day on $7.20. Page 15.

Pressure from Wilson and Horton's independent directors has caused Dublin-based news group Independent Newspapers Plc to lift its bid for the 55 percent of Wilson and Horton it does not own by 50 cents to $11. The directors support the new offer, which will now open on Thursday and close on November 8. Page

Fletcher Challenge says it could take several months to sell its indirect holding in Canadian log and lumber firm Timberwest Forest, which could be worth about C$135 million. Fletcher is not saying what it might do with the cash raised from the sale of its 26 percent indirect holding. Page 15.

Life insurance company National Mutual Holdings is set for a successful launch on the New Zealand and Australian stock exchanges today after a final issue price up to A$1.60 a share for institutional investors was set at the weekend. The $2.55 billion float is the first by a leading life insurance company in Australia and New Zealand. Page 15.

New Zealand's biggest glass company, Pilkington, does not expect to pass any cost savings on to customers after merging its Winstone Glass and Smith and Smith operations. Pilkington will shut down 20 branches and lay off 50 staff in the move.
Page 15.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Labour leader Helen Clark kept her nerve and top spot in the second and final TVNZ leaders' debate last night. Alliance leader Jim Anderton came in second, with Prime Minister Jim Bolger third. While Bolger consistently sent the worm plummeting, Clark regularly had it soaring. She scored particularly well in social policy areas and in her approach to coalitions and governing. Page 1.

Dublin-based Independent Newspapers moved swiftly to keep its take-over bid for Wilson and Horton on track by sweetening its cash offer to $11 a share. The price rise came after opposition from Wilson and Horton independent directors to the initial $10.50 bid. The directors' stand was unusual because an independent appraisal by Southpac had earlier judged the bid to be fair. Page 1.

Prime Minister Jim Bolger revived his flagging campaign with a stirring off-the-cuff speech to the Wellington Chamber of Commerce outlining what he saw as eight freedoms on the line in the general election on Saturday. At his first public outing in the last week of the election campaign, Bolger talked of the "eight freedoms" he saw as crucial to New Zealanders. They ranged from freedom from excessive taxes to freedom for individual workers to make their own decisions about union membership.

Whoever emerges as the strongest rival to ACT leader Richard Prebble in a TVNZ poll due out in the next few days will get a huge boost towards taking the Wellington Central seat. New Zealand First candidate Sarah Porter urged her supporters to cast their electorate vote for either National or Labour.

Dublin-based Independent Newspapers gave a clear indication it was aiming for 100 percent ownership of Wilson and Horton. By lifting its bid from $10.50 to $11.00 on the eve of the offer taking effect, it removed any suggestion the move was merely a tidying-up exercise.

Shares in National Mutual are tipped to reach 200 cents or higher in the first day of trading on the New Zealand and Australian stock exchanges today. Applications were received for six times the number of shares on offer, and analysts said heavy scaling back of institutional allocations should result in solid buying to support the listing.

General confidence in the outlook for the Auckland residential property market has improved strongly, according to the latest Massey University quarterly survey. Overall, a net 59 percent of real estate experts expect an improvement in the next six months.
Financial markets contrasted starkly yesterday as the New Zealand dollar dived and interest rates rose while the recent sharemarket rally gathered pace.
A record seven million passengers used Auckland International Airport in the June year, helping boost its tax-paid profit 12 percent to $39 million.

Fletcher Challenge Canada is seeking a buyer for its 52 percent stake in TimberWest Forest worth about C$270 million at the latest on-market sale price. The move is part of Fletcher Canada's effort to focus on its pulp and paper businesses, the manager of investor relations said.
